purpose: Pin what `set -e`, `set -u` and `set -o pipefail` actually do, per interpreter build, so a model of them can be checked against a measurement rather than against a reading of the specification.
note: `expected` was measured on GNU bash 3.2.57(1)-release (arm64-apple-darwin), the build Apple ships. A differing result on another build is not a failure of this corpus: it is the list of places where the option model has to carry the interpreter version. The `nounset` cases are the ones a generated program has to carry: `set -u` says an unset name and an empty one are different, and a lookup that answers an empty string for both is a program with the option silently off. The two `nounset` failures are recorded as 127 rather than 1 because this corpus runs each case through `bash -c`, and a shell that ends on an unset name reports differently there than it does reading a file — which is itself a fact about the option rather than about the harness.

cases.name: if-condition-does-not-stop
cases.script: set -e; if false; then :; fi; echo reached

cases.name: pipefail-makes-the-head-count
cases.script: set -eo pipefail; false | true; echo reached

cases.name: capturing-status-does-not-stop
cases.script: set -e; s=0; false || s=$?; echo reached

cases.name: call-site-suppresses-inside-a-function
cases.script: set -e; f(){ false; echo in-f; }; f || true

cases.name: pipefail-turns-no-match-into-failure
cases.script: set -eo pipefail; echo x | grep -q nomatch
